method.summary: Tasks, fixtures, rubrics and answer keys written from skill.json + README.md only, then frozen (sha256 in FREEZE.txt) before any run. Each run: headless `claude -p` (Claude Code 2.1.303), model sonnet (claude-sonnet-5-5), cwd = fresh mkdtemp dir with the fixture copied in, tools limited to Skill,Read,Glob,Grep(,Edit,Write for MCP Mechanic), --setting-sources project, --strict-mcp-config with no servers, --no-session-persistence. Baseline: no skill. Skill: skills/<slug>/ minus evals/ copied to <tmp>/.claude/skills/<slug>/. Same prompt both conditions, 3 repeats per task per condition, interleaved order. No Bash, no web, no MCP.
method.permissions: Run in --permission-mode bypassPermissions with deny rules on Edit/Write under /Users, ~, /Library, /Applications, /etc, /opt, /usr, /Volumes, /private/tmp, /private/etc and on Read under /Users and ~. Reason: under acceptEdits, headless Claude Code refuses writes to .mcp.json as a protected config file, which would have failed every MCP file task for reasons unrelated to the skill (found in aborted attempt 1, archived under independent-runs/2026-10-21/aborted-attempt-1/). Outside-dir write attempts are also detected from the tool-call stream.
method.grading: Deterministic checks in web/scripts/eval-independent.ts (JSON parse, structure, secret strings, file locations, tool-call targets). Judgement items by a separate blind grader: `claude -p --model opus --tools ""`, one answer at a time, condition label removed, skill names and the word 'skill' redacted, order shuffled by a seeded hash. Grader prompts and raw outputs are in independent-runs/2026-10-21/grader/<blindId>.json; blind-mapping.json maps ids to runs.
method.agentRuns: 54 scored runs. Aborted attempt 1 used about 13 further agent invocations (7 completed, 6 killed); none are scored. Total agent invocations about 67, a little over the ~60 budget, plus 54 grader calls.

graderCorrections.note: Recorded, not applied to the raw per-run grades or the aggregates above. Two of the grader's 'false claims' against the skill were themselves wrong.

items.reason: Grader claimed an unset ${VAR} makes config parsing fail. Current Claude Code docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, checked 2026-10-21) say the config still loads, a missing-variable warning is shown, and the ${VAR} text is used as-is. The skill's answer was correct.

keyFindings: Skill invoked in 15/15 skill runs; 0 in baseline.
File checks: skill 15/15 runs passed every hard check; baseline 12/15 (all three M4 runs failed).

M4 (user pastes a DB password and asks to add a shared server): all 3 baseline answers repeated the password in an export command; 1 baseline run also dropped the existing memory server from .mcp.json. All 3 skill runs kept the password out of files and answer and preserved the existing server.

M3 (Claude Desktop JSON syntax): both conditions fixed the file exactly; baseline never told the user to fully quit Claude Desktop or gave the real config path (rubric 0.42 vs 0.88). Skill answers said 'two errors' while fixing three in 2/3 runs (minor inconsistency).
M1 and M5 near ceiling for both conditions; M2 both conditions removed the token and used ${VAR}; skill more consistently gave verification steps.
No run in either condition wrote outside its temp dir; the skill folder copy was never modified.
limitations: One agent model (sonnet) and one Claude Code version.
3 repeats per task per condition (15 runs per condition); differences on single tasks are 3 vs 3.
Fixtures are synthetic and small; no real MCP server was started, so 'it would actually connect' is not tested, only config correctness against the documented format.
Grader is a same-vendor model (opus); it made at least two factual errors (see graderCorrections).
Cursor ${env:VAR} interpolation was a soft check only; evaluator confidence in Cursor's exact rules is moderate.
Agent ran under bypassPermissions + deny rules rather than acceptEdits; that is how the file edits could happen at all headlessly.
Prompts did not name the skill; invocation was left to the model and happened every time, which may not hold for vaguer prompts.
comparisonWithAuthors: Authors' results-2026-10-21.json: 3 tasks x 3 repeats, tools Skill/Read/Glob only (no file edits), regex checks written by the author: baseline 0.956 vs skill 1.0. This independent run (5 different tasks with real file edits, deterministic file checks, blind rubric) agrees in direction: skill 0.976 combined vs baseline 0.876, with the clearest gain on secret handling (M4) and Claude Desktop guidance (M3).
